dataset.name: Harmonized wood density data for Central Amazon species in the BIONTE experimental area in Manaus, Brazil
description: BIONTE (BIOmass and NuTrient Experiment) is a selective logging experiment established at the Experimental Station of Tropical Forestry (EEST, aka “ZF2”) field research station in the mid 1980s in the central Amazon (Higuchi et al. 1997, Amaral et al. 2019). The main data related to BIONTE are available as a separate dataset (Lima et al. 2022). Only species identified within the BIONTE plots were included in this dataset. Wood density, expressed in g cm-3, was collated from multiple sources that were integrated to compose the wood density for BIONTE. The starting point used was wood density data available from Chave et al. (2006), which was then adapted by Marra et al. (2016) and Marra et al. (2018). We also included data collected and synthesized by Ramírez-Méndez (2018) and Gimenez et al.(2021), who combined local estimates of wood density at the site with other sources collected in the Central Amazon. Data are included in .csv files, while BIONTE_WD_headers.txt provides descriptions of data file headers.
This dataset was originally published on the NGEE Tropics Archive and is being mirrored on ESS-DIVE for long-term archival

spatialCoverage.description: Site Name: Manaus - ZF2 BIONTE. Site ID: BR-BIO. The BIONTE (BIOmass and NuTrient Experiment) is a large-scale selective logging experiment that was established in the central Amazon at Brazil’s National Institute for Amazon Research (Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas da Amazônia – INPA) Estação Experimental de Silvicultura Tropical (EEST, aka “ZF2”) field research station in the mid 1980s. The project was designed to quantify the effects of logging disturbance intensity on forest dynamics and investigate sustainable timber harvest pathways for Amazon forests. Site contact(s): (Jeff Chambers <jchambers@lbl.gov>)

measurementTechnique: When combining data sources, multiple wood density entries for a given species or genus were included as a simple average. To assign wood density values to individuals within BIONTE, we used matching species name if available, and if not, then genus, then family; if none of these were available, we used the plot average wood density for that individual, following the same approach from Chave et al. (2006).
